text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel is not evidence of anything on its own. Panels skew in all directions by chance and by departmental composition; a four-person panel of one sex is unremarkable. Raising it as your main point makes you look aggrieved rather than credible, and it's the weakest part of your case.

Your stronger ground is substantive: the unanswered request for written reasons, the selection criteria, and how "broad experience of regulatory affairs" was weighted against your qualifications. Chase that in writing, politely, citing any internal policy or statutory deadline for reasons.

Honestly, credentials don't determine outcomes. Head-of-function roles often favour regulatory and stakeholder experience over technical depth. That may simply be what happened.
